response.sql: WITH race_avg AS (SELECT r.raceId, c.country, AVG(ds.wins) AS race_wins FROM driverStandings ds JOIN races r ON r.raceId = ds.raceId JOIN circuits c ON c.circuitId = r.circuitId GROUP BY r.raceId, c.country), country_avg AS (SELECT country, AVG(race_wins) AS avg_wins FROM race_avg WHERE race_wins IS NOT NULL GROUP BY country), bench AS (SELECT AVG(avg_wins) AS b FROM country_avg), kept AS (SELECT ca.country, ca.avg_wins FROM country_avg ca, bench WHERE ca.avg_wins > bench.b), kept_mean AS (SELECT AVG(avg_wins) AS m FROM kept) SELECT k.country, k.avg_wins AS average, k.avg_wins - bench.b AS above_overall_benchmark, k.avg_wins - kept_mean.m AS above_second_mean FROM kept k, bench, kept_mean WHERE k.avg_wins > kept_mean.m

assumptions.assumption: Per-race average is taken over all driverStandings rows for that race (each driver row counts equally), using the stored running-total wins; races with no standings rows are excluded.
The 'second mean' is the simple mean of the country averages that exceeded the overall benchmark, and the second filter is strictly above it.
